note: Where each scenario of the VM catalogue (scripts/scenarios/Weir.Scenarios.Catalog.ps1) runs once the VM is gone, in catalogue order. Read by scripts/scenarios-in-ci.mjs and checked against docs/exec-plans/active/PLAN-SCENARIOS-IN-CI.md by scripts/scenarios-in-ci.test.mjs. home: linux (Docker Compose on ubuntu-latest), windows (windows-latest) or not-portable (with the reason). state: to-port, ported (runs in CI), green-twice (passed in two CI runs on main, on different commits, with no failing run between: the VM may stop being the gate for it). passedInCi lists the CI runs a ported scenario passed in: the run, the commit and the ref it ran on. green-twice needs two of them on main, on different commits. catalogue: false marks a scenario written for CI only, for behaviour the VM suite never covered; it is not in the catalogue.

weir-only.what: Weir alone in the Docker image: films dropped into workflows with no manager.

weir-browser.what: Weir alone in the Docker image, driven through a real browser.

with-deluno.what: Weir, Deluno and the real download clients, each hand-off followed through both apps.

windows-install.what: The Windows installer on a clean runner: install, the server and its secrets, the recovery command, uninstall and reinstall.

windows-update.what: The tray updates the newest published release to this commit's build through its own update code, from a release feed made of the build's packages.

windows-tray.what: The real tray, driven through UI Automation.

windows-files.what: What the installed server does to real files on real NTFS volumes and a real network share, and the setting that opens its port to other devices.

scenarios.why: The tray updates a running install through its own code: the newest published release is installed, and a release feed made of this commit's package (the PC's hosts file points github.com at a stand-in) is checked, downloaded, verified and applied; the data, the account and the secrets survive.
Weir talks to Deluno over HTTP only, so Deluno's published image in Compose is the same Deluno.
A film Deluno hands over is followed through Weir and back; Deluno's image and the real download clients run in Compose.
Needs a release whose folder in a real download client holds a small extra, read through that client's own API.
Deluno's send-again is its own API call; both sides are read over HTTP.
Compares the outcome each app recorded for every hand-off; both are read over HTTP.
Deluno hands over a release Weir cannot read; Weir and Deluno are read over HTTP and the report between them is recorded.
Deluno hands over a release Weir rejects by its rules; Deluno refuses it and removes the download, Weir leaves it.
A hand-off Weir holds while paused is dropped by Stop waiting in Deluno; Deluno asks Weir to drop it and both are read over HTTP.
A show added by title and an episode of it sent to qBittorrent; a real Deluno hands it to Weir as TV and both are read over HTTP.
A season pack of two episodes handed to Weir by a real Deluno as one hand-off; both applications are read over HTTP.
A download deleted from its folder while Weir is paused and holds the hand-off; read through both applications.
Runs Weir-win-Setup.exe silently and starts the installed Weir.exe with its tray; a clean windows-latest runner is the clean machine.
Nothing in it is Windows: a brand-new browser context sees account creation, then sign-in. Chromium under Playwright takes the place of Edge.
The server cleans a film with the image's own ffmpeg; the first scenario ported, with the checks the VM makes.
The same server behaviour on the same image, asked to process a cleaned film again.
The server hears the tray through a file in its data folder, and that watcher is the same on Linux; the file is written in the container. The tray's side stays with windows-tray.
A file is put in a watched folder and deleted while Weir waits for it to settle; nothing in it is Windows.

Drives the real installed tray: Weir offers the buttons only while the tray is alive, each press leaves a flag file the tray takes, and the state comes to rest with an answer. Run against the release feed, as the VM did.
Runs the installed WeirServer.exe recover as a person's console does; the Docker form of the command is already proved by the Docker smoke.
The VM suite never ran the uninstaller. Weir is uninstalled twice on a clean runner, stopped and running, and the data folder, the secrets and the account must be as they were.

The VM suite never pressed a menu item. Every item of the tray menu is pressed through UI Automation on the real installed tray, with its effect on the real server, the PC and tray-host.log (which keeps every balloon).
The VM suite never ended a server. The real server is ended by its own process id three times, and again with its port taken: the tray brings it back after growing waits and logs why.
The tray gives up after five failed starts once, with the red icon and a balloon; Restart Weir brings Weir back with a fresh budget, and Quit is never answered with a start.
Change port through the real window: a move that works is saved and answers, one the server cannot make goes back and saves nothing, and both ports failing ends Stopped.
Allow other devices asks Windows for the firewall rule for real (the runner is an administrator) and restarts the server for the network; Only allow this PC takes it back.
A second Weir.exe in the same session exits 0 and leaves one tray and one server; the running tray says Weir is already running, and a silent second launch says nothing.

The starts nobody sees and the starts a person answers: no start opens the browser, a start with nobody at the desktop that cannot start Weir exits 1 and says why, a taken saved port is asked about, and WEIR_PORT is honoured.

The VM suite never cleaned a library file in place. The installed server cleans a real film at its own path on NTFS, with and without the original kept, and leaves a film another program holds open exactly as it was.

The VM suite never ended the server mid-swap. The installed server is ended by its process id at each point of the swap and started again; one intact film is left under its name and the interrupted clean finishes.
A second real NTFS volume (a virtual disk) is the output drive: a cleaned film appears at its final name only when whole, and an unchanged film is copied where a hard link is refused.
The original is kept on another real volume: copied, checked and deleted, and a crash between the steps loses neither file.
A small real volume fills during a pass: the pass waits, writes nothing, records nothing as done and completes when room returns; the unchanged-publish check does the same.
A real SMB share on the runner, used by its UNC path: folders found and used, a removed share reported and nothing lost, a restored share used again.
A share that stops answering without refusing (the SMB client talks through a relay that can stop passing data): reported unreachable, other workflows and the System page unaffected.

Other devices switched on and off through the API on the installed Weir: the listener, the firewall rule for every profile and the machine's own network address are read; a second machine is not available on one runner.
The VM suite never waited for it: in Automatic mode the tray downloads the full package and installs it by itself once Weir has been idle for 5 minutes, and not before.
The VM suite never ended a tray with an update downloaded: in Download only mode the update waits, and the next start of the tray installs it before the server starts.
The VM suite could only show 'nothing newer': a package changed after its hash was recorded is refused, and GitHub being down fails the check, each in plain words, with the old Weir still running.
